solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: I prepare to fill barrows from back to front as planned (9)

definitions.note: an adjective standing in for an adverbial phrase: a strategic move is one made as planned

indicators.note: what fills something goes inside it, so I GET goes into the barrows
read from back to front, the whole assembly runs in reverse

blocks.note: I + get, as in get the dinner ready

annotation.surface: Someone loading up wheelbarrows back to front, just as they meant to.
annotation.walkthrough: Once I GET sits inside CARTS, the whole string CIGETARTS is read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose adjectival sense: a move that serves a plan is one made as planned, as in a strategic withdrawal.

entries.clue: Numbers agents rely on uncovering when backing shop worker (11)

indicators.note: taking the cover off rely strips its outside letters, leaving EL
backing means moving backwards, so the whole string reverses

blocks.note: nos is the abbreviation for numbers
rely without its first and last letters
as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: Sales staff depending on sales figures that are only revealed as time goes on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Numbers agents rely on' reads as one phrase about sales targets; it is three separate pieces. The whole string NOSREPSELAS is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the job title covers anyone employed to sell to customers across a shop counter.

entries.clue: Trashy books I bound in haste (7)

indicators.note: something bound in is held inside, so BBI goes into the haste word

blocks.note: B is book, so BB is books, plus I

annotation.surface: A cheap paperback thrown together in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like bookbinding, which fits the books in the surface; here it means held inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal adjective: calling a film or book this means it is worthless, which is what trashy says.

entries.clue: Effort stumped by private meeting (5)

blocks.note: st. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

annotation.surface: A batsman's best effort cut short when he is stumped.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while he is out of his ground; scorecards write it as st.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a romantic flavour: the word names a secret arranged meeting, classically between lovers.

entries.clue: Westerner who shoots up, comfortable to hang around (10)

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from bottom to top, so SNUG reverses

annotation.surface: A cowboy who shoots up the town and then lingers comfortably.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoots up' reads as one phrase about gunfire; the definition ends at shoots and up belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the word names the quick-drawing gunman of Wild West films, a Westerner who shoots.

entries.clue: Thoroughly investigate containers spanning vessel (7)

indicators.note: to span something is to stretch across it, so the containers go round the vessel

blocks.note: vas is an anatomical vessel or duct

annotation.surface: Someone combing through crates that stretch across a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which fits containers; it is the anatomical word vas, a duct.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: besides seeking votes, the verb means to discuss or examine a question in detail.

entries.clue: Trap for Londoners on both sides of the Thames? (5,3,5)

definitions.text: on both sides of the Thames

blocks.note: trap is slang for mouth, and Cockney rhyming slang swaps mouth for a phrase that rhymes with it

blocks.clueFragment: on both sides of the Thames
blocks.note: the river runs east to west through London, so its two banks face opposite compass points

annotation.surface: A snare set for Londoners wherever they live along the river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trap' sounds like a snare but is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'. Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it, so mouth becomes north and south.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the rhyming-slang phrase stands for mouth, which trap also means, and the two compass points name London's two banks.

entries.clue: Type of power that’s leaner, developed with urgency (7,6)

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An energy source that has been slimmed down and pushed through in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is split by 'with', which joins the two words rather than signalling anything.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: power from splitting atoms is one type alongside solar, wind and hydro.

entries.clue: Leaves middle of nice church with wireless coverage? (9)

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, so nice gives IC
coverage wraps around, so the wireless word covers IC and CH

blocks.note: wireless is the old word for a radio

annotation.surface: Someone quitting a church halfway through because the mobile signal is poor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, departs; it is a noun, the leaves of a salad plant. The question mark flags wireless coverage as a joke about phone signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the red, bitter Italian chicory is eaten as salad leaves.

entries.clue: Bring up the writer’s French name: I’m surprised it could mean something else (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing up lifts the letters bottom to top, so the whole string reverses

blocks.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's = my

annotation.surface: Someone raising their French name and exclaiming at a double meaning.
annotation.walkthrough: MY, NOM and OH are strung together first and then the whole of MYNOMOH is read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a word sharing its form with another is liable to carry a different meaning.

entries.clue: Nobody changed lyric including cool football chant (4,3,5)

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of lyric are rearranged
including means holding inside, so NONE takes ICE into it

annotation.surface: No one on the terraces altered the words to a chant, though it is a cool one.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice One Cyril was a 1970s Tottenham Hotspur terrace chant and hit record, after full-back Cyril Knowles; 'cool' is a verb here, to ice.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by origin: the 1970s advert catchphrase was taken up on the terraces by Spurs fans.

entries.clue: Cancels record damages? (9)

blocks.note: to scratch a horse or event is to withdraw or cancel it
record here is a gramophone record, and damages are the marks a stylus or careless hand leaves in the vinyl

annotation.surface: Someone striking out a claim for recorded damages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record damages' reads as noting a sum owed; it means marks on a gramophone record.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a racing term for withdrawing an entry, and the marks gouged in vinyl by a stylus.

entries.clue: Bring together force taken from out-of-shape English (5)

indicators.note: taken from means removed from, so F comes out of UNFIT

blocks.note: UNFIT without F, the physics abbreviation for force

annotation.surface: An unfit England side having its strength drained away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like power or an army; it is just the letter F.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to join people or things into one is to bring them together.

entries.clue: Skewer boxer wearing tights and cause serious injury (11)

indicators.note: the tights are worn around the skewer and boxer, so they go inside HOSE

blocks.note: a spit is a skewer for roasting
Muhammad Ali, the crossword's standard boxer

annotation.surface: A fighter in tights skewering an opponent badly enough to hurt him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tights' reads as a boxer's kit; hose is the old word for stockings. Muhammad Ali is the crossword's usual boxer.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal verb: to hurt someone so badly they need a hospital bed is to cause serious injury.

entries.clue: Campaign launch on high times (5)

blocks.note: to lob is to launch something in a high arc
by = times, as in three by four

annotation.surface: A campaign launched in high-flying times.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like a period or the newspaper; it is the multiplication word by.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pressing politicians on behalf of a cause is campaigning.

entries.clue: Channel Islands and Mediterranean area priest turned out of school? (11)

indicators.note: turned round, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: the first three letters of Mediterranean, as in 'the Med'
a canon is a cathedral priest

annotation.surface: A priest ministering in the Channel Islands and the Med who has been thrown out of school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned out of school' reads as expelled; turned is the reversal of CIMEDACANON, and 'out of school' is the definition. The Channel Islands are British Crown dependencies off Normandy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by paraphrase: out of school means outside the academic world, and the question mark admits the stretch.

entries.clue: Gallery excused, put back in control (5)

indicators.note: someone excused is let off and leaves, so TATE goes

blocks.note: REINSTATE, put back, without TATE, the London gallery

annotation.surface: A gallery let off its duties and then restored to power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put back in' looks like the definition; 'put back' is REINSTATE, and TATE, the London art gallery, is removed from it.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the straps that steer a horse stand for control itself, as in the reins of power.

entries.clue: Flash report of transgression finishing at nine? (11)

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: a sin that goes on until eight and stops as nine comes

annotation.surface: A news flash about some wrongdoing that wrapped up at nine.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the arithmetic: a sin lasting till eight runs out when the clock reaches nine.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to give off sparks or flashes of light, and figuratively to be dazzlingly lively.

entries.clue: Prisoner with less reason, one for mercenary leaders (11)

annotation.surface: A crazier inmate standing in for the leaders of a band of hired soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With less reason' reads as a comparison of motives; it means more crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical term: the captains of hired companies in Renaissance Italy, from Italian condotta, a contract.

entries.clue: Repeat name, holding Spanish article level (7)

indicators.note: what holds something has it inside, so ECHO and N hold EL

annotation.surface: Someone repeating a name while clutching a Spanish newspaper article.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of writing; it is the grammatical article, Spanish el.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rank or tier within an organisation, originally a formation of troops.

entries.clue: Most ready for old-timer’s meeting of the mendacious? (7)

blocks.note: lief is an archaic word for willing, and old-timer's flags the old word
a gathering of liars, read as two words

annotation.surface: Veterans gathering for a reunion where everyone tells tall stories.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old-timer's' tells you the word is archaic, not that the meeting is for the elderly. The question mark flags the invented second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the archaic superlative of lief, willing, means most ready, and read as two words it is a festival of lies.

entries.clue: Rough winds in second month for grass (7)

indicators.note: to wind is to twist, so the letters of rough are twisted round
the rearranged letters go inside S and M

annotation.surface: Wild winds blowing through the grasses in February.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rough winds' reads as stormy weather and 'second month' as February; winds is a verb and second and month are separate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the tall cereal plant grown for grain and syrup is a grass.

entries.clue: Australian native “X” welcomed by Melbourne’s dame? (7)

indicators.note: someone welcomed is taken in, so EDNA takes CHI inside

blocks.note: Dame Edna Everage, Barry Humphries' character from Melbourne
X is the Greek letter chi

annotation.surface: A famous Melbourne dame greeting a mysterious Australian known only as X.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the dame as a comic creation: Dame Edna Everage, the Melbourne housewife played by Barry Humphries.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the spiny egg-laying mammal is native to Australia and New Guinea.

entries.clue: Detective’s seniority keeps equality run down (9)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so DI'S AGE holds PAR

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector, so detective's = DI'S

annotation.surface: A detective's rank protecting fair treatment within the force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run down' looks like tired or like a verb of motion; it means to belittle. DI is the standard abbreviation for a Detective Inspector.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to belittle or speak slightingly of someone is to run them down.

entries.clue: Standard warning to firefighters without face masks? (5,4,2,4,4)

definitions.text: Standard warning to firefighters without face masks?

blocks.note: reads as routine, but means a classic popular song, as in a jazz standard

blocks.clueFragment: warning to firefighters without face masks?
blocks.note: the song's title read literally is what an unmasked firefighter would be told

annotation.surface: A routine caution for firefighters who go in without breathing gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like routine; it means a well-known song, as in a jazz standard, and the song's title is exactly what the unmasked firefighter would be told.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the 1933 Jerome Kern standard's title is also the literal warning an unmasked firefighter needs.

entries.clue: Dishonestly obtaining lots without any new part required (9)

indicators.note: without any means lacking every one, so all three Ns go

blocks.note: NOBBLING, getting by underhand means, without its Ns
A TON = lots, without its N
N = new; every one is dropped

annotation.surface: Someone cheating to get a lot of something without adding any fresh parts.
annotation.walkthrough: NOBBLING A TON holds three Ns and 'without any new' removes them all. To nobble is British slang for obtaining by trickery.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: an instrumental line the composer marks as essential, a part required rather than optional.

entries.clue: Retiring, hiding skin blemish with dark complexion (7)

indicators.note: what hides something holds it out of sight inside, so SHY holds WART

blocks.note: a wart is a skin blemish

annotation.surface: A bashful person covering up a spot on their darker skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like leaving work or going to bed; it means shy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective describes a dark or dusky complexion.

entries.clue: Find the answer to upset person mislaying electric vehicle? (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so EV LOSER reads upwards

blocks.note: a loser is someone who mislays things

annotation.surface: Solving the case of someone distraught at losing their electric car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as distressed; it is the reversal. The person mislaying the EV is its loser, so EV LOSER is turned over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to settle a problem or doubt is to find the answer to it.

entries.clue: Runner in the cold not going full pelt? (3)

indicators.note: not full means cut short, so SKIN loses its last letter

blocks.note: a pelt is an animal's hide; not going full docks the final letter

annotation.surface: A jogger in winter who never quite runs flat out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Full pelt' reads as top speed; pelt is an animal's skin, docked here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the long blade a skier stands on runs over snow, so it is a runner in the cold.

entries.clue: Parisian cleric stops near an arresting person (6)

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so ABBE fills NR

blocks.note: abbé is French for a priest

annotation.surface: A French priest halting close by a striking figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' looks like striking; it means one who arrests.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal agent noun: one who nabs, collars or arrests people.

entries.clue: French man shortened cloth (6)

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the name loses its last letter

blocks.note: FABRICE, a French man's name, without its end

annotation.surface: A Frenchman whose trousers have been taken up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French man' is a first name, Fabrice, not a nationality.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: woven or knitted material is cloth.

entries.clue: Skill of two vessels flanking small isle (13)

indicators.note: vessels on each side of something flank it, so they sit either side of SMAN

blocks.note: S = small, and MAN = the Isle of Man
a ship is the second vessel

annotation.surface: Seamanship needed to keep two boats either side of a tiny island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two vessels' gives two different words, CRAFT and SHIP, one either side. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the quality of good handiwork is skill.

entries.clue: Neat square at the back, pointed at the front? (9)

definitions.text: square at the back, pointed at the front?

blocks.clueFragment: square at the back, pointed at the front?
blocks.note: the shape of a ship, square at the stern and pointed at the bow

annotation.surface: A description of a tidy object with a flat back and a pointed front.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a ship's shape, with a square stern and a pointed bow.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the idiom for orderly and tidy, and read literally, the shape of a vessel with a square stern and pointed bow.

entries.clue: Suffering from heat, wrestle with agitation (7)

definitions.note: swelter is a noun here, the state of suffering from heat

indicators.note: agitation shakes things up, so the letters of wrestle are rearranged

annotation.surface: A wrestler overheating and getting worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suffering from heat' reads like an adjective, but the answer is a noun, a state of sweaty heat.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a state of oppressive heat, or of sweating in it.

entries.clue: Fact-filled announcement of so-called garden city constructed (4-8)

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the answer sounds like the phrase
so called means named out loud, confirming a sound-alike

blocks.note: Welwyn Garden City was built in the 1920s, so it was formed

annotation.surface: A press release, packed with facts, about building a new garden city.
annotation.walkthrough: Welwyn Garden City is a planned town in Hertfordshire, north of London, pronounced 'wellin'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having plenty of knowledge is being fact-filled.

entries.clue: Extremely delicate Test India played (9)

indicators.note: played means put into action or rearranged, so the letters are shuffled

annotation.surface: A delicate Test match against India.
annotation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'played' belongs to that picture but works here on the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain superlative: dainty means delicate, so its superlative means extremely delicate.

entries.clue: Hems cut off blackish clothes once ready abroad (11)

indicators.note: off means wrong or spoiled, so the letters of hems cut are rearranged
to clothe is to wrap round, so DARK goes round the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: Hems cut off dark clothes that were ready to be sent overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' is a verb, not garments, and 'ready' is slang for cash, as in ready money.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by history: Germany's currency until the euro arrived in 2002, so once ready money abroad.

entries.clue: PA is last to employ in good time (6)

indicators.note: the last of employ is its final letter, Y

annotation.surface: A personal assistant, the last one taken on, arriving punctually.
annotation.walkthrough: 'PA' looks like a personal assistant; it is per annum, Latin for by the year.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbreviation: PA is per annum, Latin for by the year.

entries.clue: Stay on ocean (6)

blocks.note: the main is the open ocean

annotation.surface: Staying out at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to stay put is to not leave.

entries.clue: Musical group hate live sets — their covers, anyway (11)

indicators.note: a word's covers are its outside letters, so each of the three words gives its first and last

blocks.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians
outer letters of hate, live and sets

annotation.surface: A band that hates playing live, apart from cover versions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like cover versions a band plays; here it means the outside letters of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adverb means all the same, anyway.

entries.clue: Blue bloodline making the heart into pool? (10)

indicators.note: the central letter of DESCENT is turned into POND

blocks.note: DESCENT, lineage, minus its central C
a pond is a pool, put in place of the C

annotation.surface: A royal family line whose heart has been turned into a swimming pool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue bloodline' reads as an aristocratic lineage; blue is the definition, sad. The fourth of DESCENT's seven letters is its heart.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: blue in the sense of sad, low in spirits.

entries.clue: Humans advanced to get superpower (3)

blocks.note: A = advanced, as in A level

annotation.surface: Humanity evolving until it gains a superhuman ability.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Superpower' suggests a comic-book ability; it is a dominant nation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the United States is the leading superpower.

entries.clue: Number for tea party caterer? (5,3,3,6,2)

blocks.note: reads as a phone number to ring, but means a song
the nursery rhyme whose heroine gets the kettle going so everyone can have tea

annotation.surface: A number to ring for someone to cater a tea party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a phone number; it is a song, the nursery rhyme about Polly making tea.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the nursery rhyme ends 'we'll all have tea', so it is the song for a tea party.

entries.clue: Optimistic person under 5, and mostly boring any over (9)

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is under something comes after it, so the rest follows POLL
mostly means not quite all, so AND loses its last letter
to bore is to drill into, so AN goes inside
in a down entry, over turns the word upwards, so ANY reads YNA

blocks.note: 5 down is CANVASS, and to canvass is to poll
AND without its last letter, bored into YNA

annotation.surface: An optimistic toddler under five, mostly boring anyone who will listen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Under 5' looks like a child's age; the 5 points to the answer at 5 down, CANVASS, which gives POLL.
annotation.definitionFit: An eponym: the relentlessly cheerful heroine of Eleanor Porter's 1913 novel lends her name to any optimist.

entries.clue: One’s said to doctor, “Neuter cat” (9)

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A pet owner asking the vet to neuter their cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the vet being spoken to; it is a verb telling you to rearrange the quoted words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by paraphrase: the noun means something spoken, one thing a person has said.

entries.clue: Linseed’s foremost in hot, sweet bread (7)

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter
the L goes inside the word for hot

annotation.surface: A warm sweet loaf with linseed at the top of the ingredient list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot' reads as warm from the oven; it is slang for stolen.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the German Christmas fruit loaf is a sweet bread.

entries.clue: Carry by pickup, perhaps with special significance (7)

blocks.note: a microphone, of which a guitar pickup is one kind

annotation.surface: Carrying something in a pickup truck because it matters so much.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pickup' suggests a truck; it is the sound-sensing device on an electric guitar, a kind of mic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense: something that acts as an emblem or symbol is held to have special significance.

entries.clue: Liquor barrel lies north of Iowa country (7)

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
is = lies, as in 'the town is to the east'
IA is the postal code for Iowa

annotation.surface: A barrel of liquor sitting somewhere north of Iowa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lies' is not deceit but lies in place, as in 'the town lies to the east'. IA is the US postal code for Iowa.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category: the North African state between Algeria and Libya is a country.

entries.clue: Stock phrases relating to Arsenal’s top footballer (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Pundits' clichés about the best player at Arsenal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arsenal's top footballer' reads as one phrase; Eric Cantona in fact starred for Arsenal's rivals Manchester United.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Eric, the French forward, starred for Manchester United in the 1990s.

entries.clue: Knock over a preferred piece in castling? (7)

indicators.note: knocked over is turned the other way, so RAP reads PAR

annotation.surface: A chess player knocking over their favourite piece while castling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Castling' is the chess move, which makes 'piece' look like a chessman; the question mark signals a castle's parts instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the low wall along a castle's battlements is one piece of a castle.

entries.clue: Thorn Birds’ central character in difficult situation (7)

indicators.note: the central character of birds is its middle letter
the R goes inside the word for a difficult situation

blocks.note: in a pickle = in a difficult situation

annotation.surface: The heroine of The Thorn Birds caught in a dilemma.
annotation.walkthrough: The Thorn Birds is Colleen McCullough's novel; 'central character' looks like its heroine but means the middle letter of birds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small sharp spine on a plant is a thorn.

entries.clue: Sweeten listless person who’s on post-match trip (11)

definitions.note: the definition describes a person by what they are doing, with 'person' from the wordplay understood

blocks.note: a mooner is someone who mooches about listlessly

annotation.surface: A lethargic footballer who needs cheering up on a trip after the game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a football fixture; it is a marriage, so a post-match trip is a honeymoon.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: someone on the holiday that follows a wedding, the match here.

entries.clue: City in France, home of a certain Jean (cousin of Serge) (5)

definitions.text: home of a certain Jean (cousin of Serge)

blocks.note: a city in the south of France, in Occitanie

blocks.clueFragment: home of a certain Jean (cousin of Serge)
blocks.note: Jean and Serge are fabrics, not men: the cloth of jeans is named after serge from this town

annotation.surface: A French city where a man called Jean lives, with a cousin called Serge.
annotation.walkthrough: Jean and Serge look like French men's names; they are fabrics. Denim, the cloth of jeans, is named from serge de Nîmes, 'serge from Nîmes'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the city in southern France, and the town that gave denim, the cloth of jeans, its name.

entries.clue: Envision van under repair without inserting tools (11)

indicators.note: something under repair is being put back together, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Picturing a van being mended without any tools going inside it.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is medical: a non-invasive procedure puts no instruments into the body.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term: a procedure that does not enter the body is done without inserting tools.

entries.clue: Contribution to colossal amount for historic mission (5)

indicators.note: a contribution is a part of a whole, so the answer is a piece of the following words

annotation.surface: Donating a huge sum to a historic cause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mission' reads as a task; the Alamo was a Spanish mission church in San Antonio, Texas, besieged in 1836.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by history: the Spanish mission church in San Antonio, Texas, besieged in 1836.

entries.clue: Commercial management, primarily at the office? (5)

definitions.text: Commercial management, primarily at the office?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so management gives only its first letter

annotation.surface: Business management carried on mostly at a desk.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: office-based business management is admin.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the clue in full describes the paperwork side of a business, done at the office.

entries.clue: Hater on imps, possibly — or everyone? (11)

definitions.text: Hater on imps, possibly — or everyone?

indicators.note: possibly means as it might be arranged, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone who has it in for little devils, or perhaps for all people.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a misanthrope is a hater of everyone, not just imps.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue describes someone who dislikes people, imps perhaps included, or everyone.

entries.clue: Joint, not the first to cause irritation (5)

indicators.note: without its first letter, so RANKLE loses R

blocks.clueFragment: not the first to cause irritation
blocks.note: RANKLE, to cause irritation, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A sore joint, though not the first thing to annoy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not the first' reads as not the earliest cause; it removes a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the joint between foot and leg.

entries.clue: Gentle touch with slap to settle differences (4,3,4,2)
